terra.problem: Papa comments on his own delivery when he says he will not joke about the danger.
Saying the elders can breathe again presents their relief as fact. The text does not say how they react to Samuel's answer.
The text does not say whether Saul is on the elders' minds.
The elders ask whether Samuel comes in peace. The text does not say they want to know why he is there.
The sons are consecrated and invited, but the text does not say none is left outside. The youngest is later said to be tending sheep.
Jesse calls his son the youngest, but nobody says he is too young to lead.

Saying Samuel was looking at outward appearance asserts what he was considering. The LORD tells him not to consider appearance or height, but the text does not say that was why Samuel thought Eliab was the anointed.
The text does not say this happens in the afternoon.
The text says the youngest is tending sheep, but does not say that is why he was absent from the seven.
Samuel says they will not sit down to eat until the youngest arrives. That does not establish that nobody takes a seat or that the whole room is standing.
Samuel says they will not sit down to eat. The text does not say everybody stays on their feet.
The text does not say the wait for the youngest was long.
Saying the Spirit comes with the oil connects the Spirit to the oil in a way the text does not. It says Samuel anointed David and the Spirit rushed upon him from that day forward.
